item.title: Anthropic Hits Back After US Military Labels It a ‘Supply Chain Risk’
item.description: Anthropic says it would be “legally unsound” for the Pentagon to blacklist its technology after talks over military use of its artificial intelligence models broke down.

item.title: Trump Moves to Ban Anthropic From the US Government
item.description: President Donald Trump’s sudden order comes after the Defense Department pressured Anthropic to drop restrictions on how its AI can be used by the military.

item.title: OpenAI Fires an Employee for Prediction Market Insider Trading
item.description: Prediction markets like Polymarket and Kalshi are big business, and some Big Tech employees are testing boundaries by making trades based on insider knowledge.

item.title: Wall Street Has AI Psychosis
item.description: A “thought experiment” about the impacts of AI sent stocks tumbling earlier this week. It’s probably going to keep happening.

item.title: Huxe Will Give You a Personalized, Daily Audio Summary Powered by AI
item.description: The app reads your email inbox and your meeting calendar, then gives you a short audio summary. It can help you spend less time scrolling, but of course, there are privacy drawbacks to consider.

item.title: Hands-On With Nano Banana 2, the Latest Version of Google’s AI Image Generator
item.description: Google’s latest image model, Nano Banana 2, is a powerful AI photo editor that punctures reality. Well, sometimes.

item.title: ‘Uncanny Valley’: Pentagon vs. ‘Woke’ Anthropic, Agentic vs. Mimetic, and Trump vs. State of the Union
item.description: Our hosts unpack the news of the week, starting with the ongoing feud between Anthropic and the Pentagon. Plus: All you need to know about TAT-8 and undersea cables.

item.title: This AI Agent Is Designed to Not Go Rogue
item.description: The new open source project IronCurtain uses a unique method to secure and constrain AI assistant agents before they flip your digital life upside down.

item.title: How Chinese AI Chatbots Censor Themselves
item.description: Researchers from Stanford and Princeton found that Chinese AI models are more likely than their Western counterparts to dodge political questions or deliver inaccurate answers.

item.title: Are You ‘Agentic’ Enough for the AI Era?
item.description: Silicon Valley built AI coding agents that can handle most of the grunt work. Now, the most valuable skill in tech is deciding what they should do.
